headline: UK PM Keir Starmer resigns; Wes Streeting backs Andy Burnham to replace him
summary: Former health minister Wes Streeting has thrown his support behind Andy Burnham as the frontrunner to succeed Keir Starmer as the UK Prime Minister.
details: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has announced his resignation, triggering a race for the leadership of the Labour Party and the premiership.
Former health minister Wes Streeting has officially backed Andy Burnham to replace Starmer, strengthening Burnham's position as the frontrunner in the contest.
Streeting, who had previously considered running for the position himself, announced his support for Burnham in a letter posted on X on Monday.
In his letter, Streeting stated he is convinced that his ideas on 'progressive capitalism' have a place under Burnham's leadership.
Streeting urged the party to avoid exaggerating small differences and instead focus on delivering the necessary changes for the party and the country.
Nominations for the replacement of Starmer as Labour leader are set to open on July 9 and will close by mid-July.
If a contest occurs, a new leader and Prime Minister is expected to be in place by September.
caption:
A new race for 10 Downing Street begins. Wes Streeting has officially backed Andy Burnham to replace the resigning Keir Starmer.

UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has announced his resignation, triggering a race for the leadership of the Labour Party and the premiership.

Former health minister Wes Streeting has officially backed Andy Burnham to replace Starmer, strengthening Burnham's position as the frontrunner in the contest.

Streeting, who had previously considered running for the position himself, announced his support for Burnham in a letter posted on X on Monday.

In his letter, Streeting stated he is convinced that his ideas on 'progressive capitalism' have a place under Burnham's leadership.

Streeting urged the party to avoid exaggerating small differences and instead focus on delivering the necessary changes for the party and the country.

Nominations for the replacement of Starmer as Labour leader are set to open on July 9 and will close by mid-July.

If a contest occurs, a new leader and Prime Minister is expected to be in place by September.

headline_marked: At least 14 killed in [[fire at animation training centre]] in Lucknow
headline: At least 14 killed in fire at animation training centre in Lucknow
summary: The blaze broke out in the Aliganj area of India's most populous state, Uttar Pradesh, leaving mostly students dead.
details: At least 14 people, mostly students, were killed in a devastating fire at an animation training centre in Lucknow, India, on Monday.
The fire broke out in the Aliganj area of the city, which is the capital of Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state.
Television visuals showed the building engulfed in flames, with some individuals jumping from the first floor in a desperate attempt to save their lives.
Uniformed personnel were seen carrying bodies from the scene as crowds gathered nearby.
Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak described the incident as a major and saddening event, confirming the centre taught animation.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office expressed condolences to the bereaved families via a post on X.
The tragedy occurs just weeks after a hotel fire in Delhi killed more than 20 people, including over 10 foreign nationals.
The recurring incidents have raised serious concerns over fire safety norms and compliance in major Indian cities.
